title: SDK adapter onboarding and failure-mode lab playbook
author: Priya Nair
body:
Summary:
This playbook describes the recommended onboarding steps for new SDK adapter integrations, the lab exercises engineers must run to validate reliability and cost characteristics, the failure-mode matrix for common adapter faults, and canonical fixes for the most frequent production incidents. It is written for SDK engineers, integration partners, and support engineers responsible for triage and permanent fixes.

Scope and intent:
- Scope: language and platform adapters that translate a customer call surface (HTTP/GRPC/SDK) to Redwood’s runtime API (proxy, dual-write, or direct).
- Intent: reduce mean-time-to-detect and mean-time-to-fix for adapter-related incidents by standardizing tests, telemetry, and remediation.
- Exclusions: deep runtime kernel-level issues and third-party cloud provider outages (see related runbooks).

When to use this playbook:
1) New adapter onboarding (partner or internal)
2) Regression triage when adapter errors spike after a release
3) Oncall playbook for persistent, customer-facing degradations
4) Postmortem actionables for adapter-related incidents

Key components covered:
- Local lab harness (dx-adapter-lab)
- Telemetry contract and sampling expectations
- Failure-mode matrix and canonical fixes
- Oncall escalation and permanent remediation checklist
- Example snippets: CLI commands, sample JSON requests, and suggested test payloads

Readiness checklist (pre-onboarding):
- [ ] Adapter has a dedicated GitHub repo and CODEOWNERS entry
- [ ] Integration manifest (adapter.yaml) present with implementation and config fields
- [ ] Unit tests and integration tests in CI; coverage >= 60% for request/response logic
- [ ] Contract tests against the local dx-adapter-lab passing in CI
- [ ] Telemetry emission validated (see Telemetry section)
- [ ] Security review scheduled (if adapter touches customer data)

Adapter manifest (adapter.yaml) reference (example):
---
name: my-llm-adapter
version: 0.1.0
owner: team-llm-adapters
exposed_protocols: [http, grpc]
timeout_ms: 2500
retry_policy: { max_retries: 2, backoff_ms: 200 }
---
(Place this YAML in the repo root and include an example config in the README.)

Telemetry contract (required events and tags):
- Required events (all adapters must emit):
  - adapter.request.start (tags: adapter, operation, request_id, tenant_id)
  - adapter.request.end (tags: adapter, operation, request_id, tenant_id, status_code, duration_ms)
  - adapter.cache.hit/miss (tags: adapter, key_hash, upstream_model)
- Sampling guidance: 100% for error/>=95th latency; 1% baseline for successful, sub-100ms requests
- Traces: span name conventions: adapter.{operation}.start / adapter.{operation}.end; link to runtime.trace_id where available

Failure-mode matrix (synthesized from support incidents):
| Symptom | Likely root cause | Detect signal | Immediate mitigation | Permanent fix owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5xx errors from adapter | upstream runtime contract mismatch or invalid auth | 5xx rate in per-route dashboard; high adapter.request.end.status_code=500 | 1) Roll traffic to canary variant 2) Disable feature flag | adapter-owner + runtime-infra |
| Elevated p50/p95 latency | sync blocking call in adapter or unbounded retries | latency heatmap + spikes in adapter.request.end.duration_ms | Add circuit breaker / short-circuit heavy path | adapter-owner |
| Tokenization divergences (bad outputs) | incorrect prompt encoding or encoding charset mismatch | user-complaints + eval failure on golden prompts | Pin to reference encoder; flag affected versions | ml-infra + adapter-owner |
| Cache poisoning / stale KV | shared cache key collision across tenants | cache miss/hit ratio anomalies; cache.key_hash duplicates | Isolate cache per-tenant; invalidate keys | adapter-owner + platform |

Canonical fixes (quick reference):
1) 5xx due to schema drift:
   - Verify adapter request payload shape by running local contract tests: dx-adapter-lab contract run --manifest adapter.yaml
   - If schema change intentional, publish versioned manifest and add runtime compatibility shim (runtime-infra owns shim deploy).
2) High latency traced to a blocking dependency:
   - Add an asynchronous worker and return a 202 with x-retry-after for long ops (temporary).  Implement resilient buffering (kafka/queue) for persistent load patterns.
3) Intermittent auth failures:
   - Rotate short-lived credentials; add token refresh path and backpressure on 401 to avoid thundering herd.
4) Output regressions after adapter update:
   - Run regression suite against golden prompts: ./scripts/regression-check.sh --golden ./goldens/default.json; revert and bisect commits to find regression.

Oncall: step-by-step triage (first 20 minutes):
1) Identify scope: check per-route dashboard and ping oncall channel if >5 customers affected.
2) Quick checks (use dx-adapter-detect):
   - dx-adapter-detect --route my-adapter --window 10m --metrics [5xx, p95, throughput]
   - If 5xx > 0.5% of requests: switch to fallback adapter via runtime routing policy.
3) Capture traces: search traces by request_id from error logs and attach three examples to PagerDuty ticket.
4) Implement fast rollback or temporary traffic-split (50/50) to a previous adapter version.
5) If fix requires code change, create a hotfix branch and follow hotpatch checklist in CI (quick release with forced integration tests and manual approval).

Permanent remediation checklist (post-incident):
- Write a short postmortem and link to the incident ticket (owner: adapter-owner).
- Add or extend canonical regression tests with the failing payloads.
- Update the adapter.yaml version and document the compatibility rationale.
- Add a telemetry golden (synthetic trace) to the nightly contract run.
- Where appropriate, add a canary gate in the deployment pipeline to block regressions.

Lab exercises (must pass before acceptance to staging):
1) Failure injection: simulate 10% of upstream 500 responses and ensure adapter backpressure logic reduces retries and logs meaningful error codes. Command: dx-adapter-lab inject --mode upstream-500 --rate 10
2) Latency profiling: run 10k requests with 95th target < 250ms. Command: dx-adapter-lab load --concurrency 50 --requests 10000 --assert p95<250
3) Cost profiling: run tokenized load to measure average tokens per request and estimated cost using cost-sim tool.
4) Regression validation: run golden prompt suite and assert no semantic drift beyond allowed thresholds (see regression-check script).

Example diagnostics and snippets:
- Sample request JSON (generation):
{
  "operation": "generation",
  "model": "gpt-redwood-0.1",
  "prompt": "Summarize the following text...",
  "max_tokens": 128
}

- CLI commands:
  - Contract test: dx-adapter-lab contract run --manifest adapter.yaml
  - Local sandbox: dx-adapter-lab sandbox --port 8081 --env local
  - Trace fetch: runtime-cli traces fetch --filter \"service:adapter and request_id:1234\" --output sample-trace.json

Observability dashboards to check (links internal):
- Adapter per-route SLO dashboard: /dashboards/adapter-per-route
- Telemetry golden traces: /dashboards/adapter-golden-traces
- Latency heatmap and error breakdown: /dashboards/adapter-latency-errors

Operational knobs and defaults (table-like list):
- timeout_ms: 2500 (default)
- max_retries: 2 (sensible default for idempotent ops)
- circuit_breaker_threshold: 5 failures / 1m window
- cache_ttl_seconds: 60 (per-tenant isolation recommended)

Guidelines for SDK authors (best practices):
- Keep adapter code idempotent for at-least-once retry modes.
- Prefer async paths for non-critical enrichment work.
- Emit structured logs with request_id and version tag.
- Add a compatibility test that asserts the adapter honors runtime feature flags.

Escalation and ownership map:
- Adapter runtime faults (5xx / contract drift): adapter-owner -> runtime-infra -> eng-sre
- Security-sensitive regressions: adapter-owner -> security -> legal (per policy)
- Billing/cost regressions: adapter-owner -> finance -> product (to evaluate pricing impact)

Acceptance criteria for production rollout:
1) All lab exercises green and artifacts uploaded to artifact store.
2) Telemetry contract tests pass in nightly CI for two weeks with synthetic traffic.
3) SLO smoke tests show p50<120ms, p95<250ms for baseline traffic.
4) Post-release monitoring runbook is documented in the repo README.

FAQ (short):
Q: What if my adapter requires specialized model tokens or encoding?
A: Document the encoding in adapter.yaml, add an adapter-specific token-metering test, and notify runtime-infra to add a feature flag.

Q: How do we handle large-batch requests that exceed 2.5s?
A: Use the async buffer pattern with 202 responses and a status check endpoint; update manifest.timeout_ms accordingly.

Appendix A — quick regression-check.sh (example):
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -e
GOLDEN=\"./goldens/default.json\"
FAIL=0
for p in $(jq -c '.prompts[]' $GOLDEN); do
  out=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8081/generate -d \"${p}\")
  # simple heuristic compare: contains expected keyword
  expected=$(echo $p | jq -r '.expected')
  echo \"Checking prompt expected=${expected}\"
  if ! echo $out | grep -q \"${expected}\"; then
    echo \"Mismatch for prompt: ${p}\"
    FAIL=1
  fi
done
if [ $FAIL -eq 1 ]; then
  echo \"Regression checks failed\"
  exit 2
fi
